The Moon is at an altitude of **10.813 degrees**. In practical terms, this means it is about 11 degrees above the horizon.

*   Since the sky is clear, an object 11 degrees up is well above the "ground clutter" (trees, houses, or hills) unless you are in a very dense urban center or a deep valley.

### 2. The Azimuth (Direction)
The azimuth is **86.037 degrees**. 
*   In navigation, 0° is North, 90° is East, 180° is South, and 270° is West.

*   Because it is only 10 degrees up, it will be low in the sky, but it will be distinct against the night sky.

*   **Sky Condition:** You noted the sky is **clear**, which is the most important factor for visibility.
